question: Should transcribecpp be added as an optional stt_provider because Metal Parakeet TDT 0.6B v2 (ggml, Q8_0) beats sherpa-parakeet CPU (int8 onnx) on the same fixtures? (WI-26ae84 spike 1)

criteria_fixed_in_advance.accuracy: mean transcript_score >= sherpa-parakeet on the same fixtures
criteria_fixed_in_advance.latency: median stt_final_ms <= sherpa-parakeet, compared on the same basis
criteria_fixed_in_advance.reliability: runs_without_a_final_transcript == 0 and no caption hallucinations on non-speech fixtures
criteria_fixed_in_advance.backend_honesty: the artifact records the backend that actually ran; a Metal run that silently fell back to CPU is not a Metal win
criteria_fixed_in_advance.decision_rule: add the optional provider only if all hold; the default stays sherpa-parakeet either way (flip is a later PR after a second run)

cpu_sanity.note: ggml CPU is 1.4x slower than sherpa int8 CPU; the win is Metal, not ggml

result.decision: ADD transcribecpp as an optional stt_provider (Metal passes every gate). Default stays sherpa-parakeet; a default flip needs a second T1-style run in the live pipeline per spec/20.

reading_the_numbers: Accuracy is identical to four decimals (0.9645 both) - same weights, two runtimes, so the gap collapsing to 0.0 is the expected result and a useful sanity check on the driver. The latency win is real but bounded: Metal decodes an utterance in 28.1 ms median vs 86.5 ms for sherpa CPU (3.1x), but on the realtime basis the full STT-final path medians 2812 ms because utterance length plus the VAD silence floor dominates. Adding the provider buys ~60 ms of perceived latency today; the durable value is GPU offload (CPU freed for brain/TTS) and 3x decode headroom for longer utterances. ggml CPU (118.8 ms) is slower than sherpa int8 CPU - transcribe.cpp earns its place only when Metal/CUDA actually runs.
evidence_limits: Latency was compared on a compute-only basis: control ran with --fixture-realtime=false, candidate numbers are the CLI's per-file mel+encode+decode with the model loaded once per batch (load ~200-270 ms excluded). The realtime control run (median 2812 ms) is recorded in provenance to anchor the basis gap. An in-pipeline provider would add a temp-wav write per utterance (the whispercpp seam); that cost is not measured here.

The L4 wavs were never committed; fixtures were re-synthesized from scripts/stt-ab-fixtures.txt (4 recoverable L4 texts + 10 new same-style texts). Internally valid - both providers saw identical wavs - but absolute numbers are not comparable to L4's (its realtime median was 4580 ms on longer utterances).

spec/20 named tests/voiceflow/testdata as the non-speech pair, but barge_in.wav contains the spoken word 'Okay'; the driver generates deterministic silence and noise fixtures instead. sherpa-parakeet never opens VAD on them (stt timed out), so the hallucination comparison is CLI-only: both backends returned empty text on all 12 non-speech runs.

Metal was requested explicitly (--backend metal, never auto). Honesty evidence is indirect: encode_ms distributions differ clearly from the cpu runs (18-25 ms vs 80-140 ms) and the build's contract.json lane is metal; the CLI errors on unavailable backends rather than falling back.
This record was assembled from two cmd/stt-ab invocations (one per candidate) plus the non-speech and realtime raw files; provider blocks are verbatim aggregator output.
durable_value: First measured proof that ggml Parakeet on Metal beats the shipped sherpa CPU path at equal accuracy on this machine class - the number E2 (offline provider) is justified by. Also fixes the fixture gap: the A/B texts are now committed (scripts/stt-ab-fixtures.txt) and the driver (cmd/transcribecpp-ab + scripts/stt-ab-transcribecpp.sh) regenerates wavs and records deterministically, so the pre-default-flip second run is a one-command rerun.

provenance.fixtures: synthetic (14 utterances re-synthesized from scripts/stt-ab-fixtures.txt via cmd/golden-tts af_heart 0.95, resampled to 16 kHz mono, 1.5 s trailing silence) + 2 generated non-speech (silence, fixed-seed noise)
provenance.command: scripts/stt-ab-transcribecpp.sh (control: obey-voice benchmark --stt-provider sherpa-parakeet --fixture-realtime=false; candidate: transcribe-cli --batch --batch-jsonl via cmd/transcribecpp-ab)
provenance.latency_basis: compute-only: control --fixture-realtime=false STTFinalElapsed; candidate mel+encode+decode ms, model loaded once per batch

realtime_control_anchor.note: same fixtures with --fixture-realtime=true; the audio + VAD floor the compute basis strips out

backend.requested: metal and cpu, each requested explicitly via --backend (never auto)
backend.observed_evidence: indirect for these numbers. The CLI does echo the executing lane ('parakeet: using metal backend: MTL0' / 'using cpu backend (strict)', and a 'backend:' summary line), but this run used -q --batch-jsonl, which suppresses that line and emits no backend field, so the driver captured no per-run confirmation. What supports the labels: --list-devices lists a metal GPU and a CPU device on this machine, the echo was verified out-of-band on the same binary and flags, and the two runs differ 4.2x in decode time

transcribecpp.built: cmake from source (examples/cli transcribe-cli), macOS arm64, metal+cpu lanes
transcribecpp.release_tarball_note: upstream release assets ship only the native libraries; the CLI is an examples/ cmake target

model.quant_note: Q8_0 vs control int8 onnx - quant held near-lossless so runtime is the variable under test

provenance.hand_assembled: provider blocks verbatim from cmd/stt-ab; multi-candidate merge and prose by hand (single-candidate tool)
